articles.title: phpAfterShell Explained: How Hackers Could Turn a PHP Session Flaw Into Code Execution
articles.summary:
PHP's default file-based session storage can be made to return objects an attacker chose, by cutting off a session write at the right moment. When combined with a second weakness, such as a suitable gadget chain in the app, those objects can allow the attacker to run code on the server.

Today's PHP releases fix the flaw, called phpAfterShell.

articles.title: Critical VMware vCenter Flaw (CVSS 9.8) Lets Network Attackers Bypass Authentication
articles.summary:
A critical flaw in VMware vCenter lets an attacker with network access bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to the system, Broadcom, which owns VMware, said in an advisory published today.

Fixed versions are out for all supported branches, and the company lists no workaround. vCenter is the central console for managing an organization's ESX hosts and virtual machines.

articles.title: Drupal Patches Critical Installer Flaw That Could Give Unauthenticated Attackers Control of Sites
articles.summary:
Under specific conditions, a critical vulnerability in Drupal core can allow an attacker without login credentials to use the built-in installer to attempt to reinstall a site.

That can lead to a site takeover or remote code execution, and the project rates the vulnerable configurations as uncommon. Fixed releases for all supported branches shipped yesterday.

articles.title: Everything Is a Web Application, Including Your Firewall
articles.summary: One of the early targets of PHP2Shell exploitation was the firewall. On October 28, Palo Alto Networks confirmed that attackers were exploiting the two PHP vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, against PAN-OS management interfaces exposed to the internet. Both flaws let anyone execute code on the web server without authentication. The disclosure itself went a little wrong.

articles.title: Hackers Breach N-able Cloud Server, Disrupting Email Security Management Across 3 Regions
articles.summary:

articles.title: Ruby Releases Fixes for 7 Regex and String Flaws, Warns 5 Have Proof-of-Concept RCE
articles.summary:
Ruby contains seven memory-safety flaws in its regular expression engine and its string case-conversion code. For five of them, its maintainers say, proof-of-concept exploits, or PoCs, have shown that crafted input can run code on the machine.

"We are aware of PoCs that prove some of them can be used to trigger remote code execution," the maintainers said.

articles.title: Researcher Demonstrates Database RCE Exploits Affecting PostgreSQL, MySQL and Oracle
articles.summary:
